extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and editors of scientific journals (researchers who perform manuscript review)
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist of criteria and considerations for evaluating the quality, integrity, and publishability of scientific manuscripts during peer review. Covers methodological reproducibility, novelty, presentation, ethics/conflicts, and fit for journal readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest / Funding influence
rubrics_metrics.description: For sponsored research, did the funding source influence access to data, writing of the manuscript (e.g., employees as authors), or the decision to publish? Are any undisclosed conflicts of interest suspected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the study received support from an industry or organization that could have directly or indirectly influenced how the results are presented, interpreted, or discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundancy / Plagiarism / Self-Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manuscript appear to duplicate already published work? Is this an incremental manuscript that adds marginally to already published data without acknowledging the relationship? Is the manuscript simply a translation of published work in another language?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether there are studies by the same author or others that provide evidence of redundancies, such as similar text passages, duplicate subjects, piecemeal outcomes, or if the manuscript is published in a different language. Verify that figures and tables are original and inspect for content copied from elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific value / Contribution to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the contribution meaningful? Does the paper, by itself, make a sufficient contribution to our understanding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the manuscript is, in principle, publishable based on its contribution to the field and whether it makes a sufficient marginal contribution relative to existing work or working papers in circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper a useful original contribution? Does the manuscript address something new and add something to the existing literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the problem, goal, or intended result is new, whether it has been built or solved before, or whether it is a trivial variation or extension of previous results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance / Significance / Importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the significance of the present results described? What is the overall significance of this study? Is the topic important enough?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the scientific merit by evaluating relevance to the field, statistical significance, importance of the results, and overall interest of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation / Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript concise and understandable? Is the paper well structured with logical organization and flow?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify parts that should be reduced, eliminated, expanded, or added. Check whether the manuscript follows the standard structure of scientific writing (IMRAD where appropriate) and is well-organized with coherent prose, appropriate scholarly vocabulary, and grammar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar / Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there sentences that are not understandable? Are there typographical errors? Are the grammar and syntax correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for excessive grammatical errors that hinder understanding and determine whether the manuscript requires a professional translator or language editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Are trade names, abbreviations, symbols misused? Are terms sufficiently defined?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for inconsistent or unnecessary use of abbreviations or jargon, ensure inclusion of definitions of key terms, and verify that abbreviations are defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic / Argument flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a logical flow in the manuscript? Is the argumentation coherent across sections?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the argument flow is logical and whether there are smooth transitions between all sections so the structure and style allow clarity of logical thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality / Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the quality of the writing effective, clear, concise, and intelligible? Is there unnecessary repetition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper is written well enough so the technical content can be evaluated; note repetition that can be eliminated and whether the style is direct and appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the manuscript be interesting for a large proportion of the journal’s audience? Will the subject matter be of interest to the journal audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript's content, theme, or topic aligns with the interests of the journal's readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope / Fit for the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript content consistent with the mission and scope of the journal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether the scope of the manuscript is consistent with that of the journal and suitable for its audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness / Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper concise, or could it be shortened to make it more readable? Is the paper too long?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether the presentation of the study is succinct and identify opportunities to shorten text to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias / Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there any obvious biases created by the procedures used? Is the presentation of the results balanced and unbiased?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether there is any bias in the study, evaluate the potential impact of the bias, and determine whether it favors or opposes the expected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / Methods transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the study reproducible? Could the study be replicated on the basis of the description provided?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the article contains all necessary information (methods, protocols, analysis details) to guarantee the reproducibility of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the study data provided within the manuscript or supplementary information files?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that data required to evaluate or reproduce the work are available in the manuscript, supplements, or public repositories as appropriate.
